## Survey open-0: LIN-4456 @ cfd152fa4

`origin/main` has moved from the ticket's grounding commit 4b5001ddf to cfd152fa4 (LIN-4453, docs only). `lib/dispatch-factory.js` hasn't changed: the comment is still at 925–934, the check at 948, and the factory entry is still Waiting #8 in `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md`.

**Why this is harder than "small" suggests: the plan puts the declaration in the wrong place.**

The plan says Linear "declares `testTransport` where its transport is swapped", in `routes/test.js` and `tests/fixtures/hermetic-linear.js`. But neither file swaps anything on the provider. Both call `setLinearFetchImpl` (`lib/linear-fetch.js`), which is a module-level hook. So declaring the capability "there" means each installer has to set a flag on the `linearProvider` singleton (`lib/providers/linear/index.js:2463`). That causes three problems:

1. **The swap happens in more places than those two.** About 40 test files call `setLinearFetchImpl` or `installHermeticLinearTransport`. One is `tests/unit/dispatch-issue-access.test.js` itself, which installs its own counting transport (lines 131–145). Its main witness, "Linear with test-token makes no transport call", would turn red unless every ad-hoc swap also sets the flag. A file that imports a route without installing anything would go back to sending `test-token` to the network, which is the LIN-1880 leak.
2. **The two swaps don't mean the same thing.** The e2e transport answers *only* `test-token` with a 401 and passes other tokens through. The hermetic fixture refuses *every* token. "My transport is swapped" is not the fact the factory needs. The fact it needs is "under NODE_ENV=test, `test-token` is not a working credential for this provider", and that is a fixed property of Linear. It doesn't depend on whether a transport has been installed.
3. **Mutating at install time makes the answer depend on order and process state.**

**What I'd do first:** decide where the declaration lives before writing code. I recommend a static field on the provider class, `testTransport = true` on `LinearProvider`, read by the factory as `provider.testTransport && isHermeticTestToken(token)`. Today's behaviour stays the same, with no installer edits. All three witnesses become plain provider objects: `linearProvider`, `LocalProvider`, and a stand-in with the field set. Then post on LIN-4447 that the plan's "declare it at the swap sites" is being changed and why, as the ticket asks.

**Smaller traps:**

- `ProviderInterface` already has a *method-keyed* `capabilities` / `supports()` descriptor (`lib/providers/interface.js:175`). Don't put `testTransport` in it, because it isn't a method and descriptor consumers enumerate it. That leaves "capability" meaning two things, so say which one you mean in the replacement comment.
- `lib/should-mock-ai.js:20–26` (`isHermeticTestToken`'s doc) says "the dispatch factory adds its own Linear-only condition". That clause goes stale in the same change.
- `tests/unit/dispatch-leftover-answer.test.js:32` quotes the Waiting #8 text as a fixture. Removing the entry doesn't break it, but don't edit it, because it is recorded wording.
- Reword the access test's `describe` title and header (lines 10–13).
- No Lesson mentions this check, and Lessons are 4,269 bytes.

**Is this a symptom of something deeper?** Somewhat. The real tangle is that "test mode" is spread across `isHermeticTestToken`, `credentialFor`'s mock data, `shouldMockAi` and the Linear fetch hook. This piece rightly fixes one; don't grow it into unifying them.

## Survey global: LIN-4456 @ cfd152fa4

Since 4b5001ddf, only a docs-only commit (LIN-4453) has landed.

**Where it lands.** The change goes in `resolveIssueAccess` in `lib/dispatch-factory.js` (1,408 lines). It also touches Linear's two test transports and Waiting 8 in `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md`. This spot is in good shape. All lanes come in through one `issueAccess` seam. `tests/unit/dispatch-issue-access.test.js` already checks witnesses 1 and 2, plus the control case (Linear with a real token reaches the transport). Only the stand-in provider is new. The area as a whole is in worse shape: it has 20 Waiting entries and a 4,530-line store. This piece is one of the few that clears a Waiting entry without growing anything.

**The obvious way has a gap.** The plan says to declare `testTransport` "where its transport is swapped", meaning `routes/test.js` and `tests/fixtures/hermetic-linear.js`. That would make each installer set a flag on the shared `linearProvider`. But Linear's swap point is `setLinearFetchImpl` (`lib/linear-fetch.js`), and three kinds of code call it, not two:
- `installTestTokenLinearTransport` (server.js:1261)
- `installHermeticLinearTransport` (35 test files)
- **5 test files that call `setLinearFetchImpl` directly**, including `dispatch-issue-access.test.js`, the test for "Linear with test-token makes no transport call".

If the installers set the flag, that witness goes red. Any test with no installer would then send `test-token` to api.linear.app, and native fetch gets past `network-guard.js`. The flag would also stay set after `restore()` unless someone clears it. A flag set by test setup makes the skip depend on test order, which is worse than the name check.

**Recommendation:** declare it statically on `LinearProvider` (`get testTransport() { return true }`). The comment should point at both installers. It only acts together with `isHermeticTestToken`, which is already gated on `NODE_ENV=test`. This changes the plan's wording, so it needs a comment on LIN-4447.

**Avoid a second copy.** Don't add `testTransport` to `PROVIDER_SURFACE` or `ui`. Both are derived from methods, so it would show up in `getCapabilities()`. Make it a plain property, like `addProvider`. Add one predicate beside `readsIssues` in `lib/as-asked-seal.js`, which is where the factory's other access rule lives.

**Who else has to learn about it.** No check I found reads any of these:
- `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md`: drop Waiting 8. Lessons is 4,258 B and no lesson clause mentions this, so nothing else there changes.
- `docs/architecture/source-map.md:216`: "including Linear with the hermetic `test-token`".
- `lib/should-mock-ai.js:21–23`: "the dispatch factory adds its own Linear-only condition".
- The factory's own comment, which this piece retires.

`tests/unit/dispatch-leftover-answer.test.js:32` quotes the Waiting text as a fixture string. It doesn't read the doc, so it stays green and needs no change.

**Better, and affordable here:**
- the static declaration
- one predicate
- the stand-in witness
- a fourth witness: Linear with `test-token` and *no* installer still makes no call
- fixes to the three pieces of stale prose

**Better still, but not this task's.** The provider name check is a symptom. The cause is production code branching on a test credential. `=== 'test-token'` appears inline at about 16 production sites (`routes/proxy-compute.js` ×7, `server.js` ×3, `task-chat`, `workspace-api-steps`, `workspace-api-audit`, `routes/test.js`), right beside the single helper that only two production modules import. If tests injected the transports instead of production code recognising the token, both this flag and those checks would go away. That spans several areas.

## Decision: where `testTransport` is declared (LIN-4456), settled as an engineering call

**Decision:** declare `testTransport` once, as a fixed property of the Linear provider (the `static` option of ruling `lin4456-testtransport-placement`). Do not set a flag in `routes/test.js` or `tests/fixtures/hermetic-linear.js`.

**Why this is an engineering call, not John's:** the words quoted from the ask ("declare it in routes/test.js and tests/fixtures/hermetic-linear.js") are the breakdown's wording of the plan, not part of John's ask on LIN-4447. They name a placement, not an outcome. The outcome John asked for is "each rule has one home, and the copies are gone", and the parent plan already says to change course where the code shows the plan is wrong. What decides the placement is code quality and coherence, which is the Principle 0 test.

**Evidence (from the worker's survey of origin/main cfd152fa4):** both installers only call `setLinearFetchImpl`, which replaces one shared module-level fetch function. A flag set there at install time would (1) turn the `dispatch-issue-access` witness ("Linear with test-token makes no transport call") red, and (2) let any test that installs no transport send `test-token` to the network again (the LIN-1880 leak), with the result depending on test order. A fixed fact of the Linear provider has neither problem and keeps the rule in one place.

**What this does not change:** the size stays "just the task"; the `provider.name === 'linear'` check and its comment are still retired; the four witnesses in the ticket stay, plus the extra one the worker proposed (Linear with `test-token` and no installed transport still makes no call).

**Record:** the ruling stays open for John only so he can see it; a suggested answer (`static`) is attached. Nothing waits on it. If John answers `installers`, that would reopen this piece, and the cost is the red witness and the leak above.

## LIN-4456 (piece 6): PR open, CI green

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2426 (targets main, head `dc7ac6f97`)

Commits on the branch, on top of `origin/main` cfd152fa4:
- `321d1f983` LIN-4456: test transport keyed on a declared capability (piece 6): the production change and the witnesses
- `dc7ac6f97` LIN-4456: docs for the testTransport capability (piece 6): Waiting #8 removed, source-map wording updated

CI (`.github/workflows/test.yml`, run 43451423774), all 8 checks pass on `dc7ac6f97`:

- Unit tests (proxy, clock +400d): pass
- E2E shards 1/4, 2/4, 3/4, 4/4: pass

Not merged. Merging is the orchestrator's or a human's.

## Review — LIN-4456

Reviewed PR #2426 at head `dc7ac6f972591d5dc62c1770202f4e3f64e60080` (`dc7ac6f97`), based on `cfd152fa4`. `origin/main` is now `92676b1fe` (LIN-4446). That commit touches none of these files except an unrelated part of `source-map.md`, and `git merge-tree` against current main merges cleanly.

CI: green. All 8 checks pass on `dc7ac6f97`: Unit, Unit (proxy, clock +400d), E2E 1–4/4, Secret scan, CI success.

### Against what was asked
- **"A provider declares `testTransport` where its transport is swapped: Linear, in `routes/test.js` and `tests/fixtures/hermetic-linear.js`."** This is narrowed on purpose. It is declared once in the `LinearProvider` constructor (`lib/providers/linear/index.js:2287`). The cut is recorded in the size record. The engineering call is comment 44b575a3. The required note on the parent exists as LIN-4447 comment 40d7c83a, so it is not a duplicate. Ruling `lin4456-testtransport-placement` is open for visibility, with `static` recommended. I checked the evidence for the cut: both installers only call `setLinearFetchImpl`, and the access test installs its own transport. An install-time flag would turn that witness red.
- **"The factory skips access only for `provider.testTransport && isHermeticTestToken(token)`."** Met. See `refusesHermeticToken` in `lib/as-asked-seal.js`, called from `resolveIssueAccess`.
- **"Do not remove a non-Linear provider's access merely because it uses `test-token`."** Met. LocalProvider and the undeclared stand-in keep access.
- **Retires: the name test and the "this is not a capability" comment.** Both are gone from `lib/dispatch-factory.js`. **Settles Waiting 8:** the entry is removed, taking Waiting from 21 to 20 entries.
- **Witnesses.** All four are present, plus a fifth: Linear with no installed transport opens no socket. The seal and file-pointer tests are in the same file and pass, and CI covers the rest.
- **Binding constraints.** No provider or GitHub reads are added and nothing about readiness is stored. Lessons are 4,269 B, under the 6,144 B cap, and no Lesson clause mentions this check. The recorded fixture in `dispatch-leftover-answer.test.js` is untouched. `testTransport` is kept out of `capabilities`, `PROVIDER_SURFACE` and `ui`. The PR body says what it retires.

### Regression check
`git log -6` on each touched file. The Linear-only skip came from LIN-4361 (93a37ab68). Its purpose was that other providers keep `test-token` as a working credential, and that is preserved and pinned by the LocalProvider and undeclared stand-in witnesses. No reverts touch these files.

### Mutation checks (run by me, each reverted, tree clean)
- I removed `this.testTransport = true` from LinearProvider. Red: "Linear with test-token makes no transport call" and "no installed transport… no socket".
- I made the predicate token-only. Red: the LocalProvider converse test and the undeclared stand-in test.
- I put the name check back (`name === 'linear'`). Red: the declaring stand-in test.
- I removed the skip entirely. Red: 3 tests, including the socket guard.

On the PR head, `tests/unit/dispatch-issue-access.test.js` passes 10/10.

### Isolated, or one of a class?
The class is "production code branching on the hermetic `test-token`". The global survey found about 16 inline `=== 'test-token'` sites (`routes/proxy-compute.js`, `server.js`, etc.). These are **outside** this ticket: they are different rules, and the Constraints explicitly bar unifying test mode here. Production behaviour is right today because `isHermeticTestToken` is gated on `NODE_ENV=test`. Home: Waiting entry in `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md` only if the LIN-4447 pieces don't already cover it; no ticket, since nothing is broken. Within this rule the change is isolated. Providers come from registry singletons, and no wrapper or spread copy of `linearProvider` reaches `issueAccess`. I checked every caller in `lib/dispatch-entrance.js` and `routes/workspace-api-feedback.js`.
`Retires:` there is no builder `### Leftovers` comment on this ticket. The PR body's "What it retires" names Waiting #8, and the diff does remove it.

### Fix for close-out (wording only, inside scope)
Two comments still describe the placement the build rejected:
1. `lib/as-asked-seal.js:111-112`, in the `refusesHermeticToken` doc: change "(a plain property on its class, set where its transport is swapped under test)" to "(a plain, fixed property declared on the provider class: Linear, in its constructor)".
2. `tests/unit/dispatch-issue-access.test.js:10-11`, in the header: change "(a plain property, set where that provider's transport is swapped under test)" to "(a plain, fixed property declared on the provider class)".

### What CI Did Not Prove
CI covers the deliverable; ledger empty. The change only takes effect under `NODE_ENV=test`, so production is unaffected. CI's unit, hermetic-proxy and E2E arms exercise every path it touches.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger. The ledger is empty. The only condition is the two wording fixes above.

## Blind read
Verdict: same. Better: the `provider.name === 'linear'` test-token skip in `lib/dispatch-factory.js` becomes one named predicate (`refusesHermeticToken`, `lib/as-asked-seal.js`), and a new test in `tests/unit/dispatch-issue-access.test.js` proves it follows the declared property, not the name (it fails at the base). Worse: the fact is just as Linear-only as before, but it now sits on the production `LinearProvider` class (`lib/providers/linear/index.js`, `testTransport = true` on every instance), and nothing ties it to the transport swaps it describes; the seal module also picks up test-mode knowledge its own header says belongs to the factory.

Read: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2426 at `dc7ac6f97` against `cfd152fa4`.

### Inside the area, fix-sized
- `lib/as-asked-seal.js` (other-features): the module header still says "lib/dispatch-factory.js decides when there is no access" and lists its provider-I/O exports as `readsIssues`, `readIssueRaw` and `writeIssueDescription`, but part of that decision (`refusesHermeticToken`, which brings in an import of `should-mock-ai.js`) now lives here. Fix: either move `refusesHermeticToken` next to `resolveIssueAccess` in `lib/dispatch-factory.js`, the only caller, or add it to the header's list and drop the "the factory decides" sentence.
- `tests/unit/dispatch-issue-access.test.js` (unmapped; concerns `lib/dispatch-factory.js`, runs-and-dispatch): the `countingProvider` comment ("The declared capability is a plain property") and the new describe title ("the testTransport capability, not the provider name") call `testTransport` a capability. `lib/providers/linear/index.js` says it is deliberately not one (not in `capabilities`, `supports()`, PROVIDER_SURFACE or `ui`). Fix: call it a "declared property" in both places.

### Inside the area, larger
- `lib/providers/linear/index.js` (providers): `this.testTransport = true` claims something that is only true where `routes/test.js` `installTestTokenLinearTransport` or `tests/fixtures/hermetic-linear.js` has swapped the transport. No test or guard links an installer to the flag. So a future installer for another provider (or a change to Linear's) can drift silently, and the decision is still per-provider by hand, under a new name. Closing that needs a decision on where test transports get registered (for example, installers that declare which provider they cover, plus a census test), and it spans providers, web-routes and test fixtures. It is larger than a fix.

### Outside the area
None.

Accept the cut: declare it as a fixed property on the Linear provider, outside the method-based capability list

— Ruling recorded via Harbour

## Close-out — LIN-4456

**Merged:** [PR #2426](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2426), squash `e8e92d50a`, pinned to head `dd0078a5f` (`--match-head-commit`). Docs-only follow-up [PR #2428](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2428), squash `0092d8d9e`, pinned to `2f7819d86`.

**What it does (review's account stands):** `LinearProvider` declares `testTransport = true` once in its constructor. `resolveIssueAccess` skips access only for `provider.testTransport && isHermeticTestToken(token)`. The `provider.name === 'linear'` test and the "this is not a capability" comment are retired, and Waiting #8 is removed. Local and undeclared stand-in providers keep `test-token` as a working credential.

**CI:** green on the exact commit merged: all 8 checks on `dd0078a5f` (Unit, Unit proxy clock +400d, E2E 1–4/4, Secret scan, CI success), run 43457097939. `main` Tests on the merge commit `e8e92d50a` also passed. PR #2428: all 8 checks green on `2f7819d86`.

### Changes I made after the approval (nobody re-read these)
- `ecd7e7d30` — review line 1 (`lib/as-asked-seal.js:111-112` doc) and line 2 (`tests/unit/dispatch-issue-access.test.js:10-11` header): both now say "a plain, fixed property declared on the provider class". Blind read, header disagreement: I **moved `refusesHermeticToken` (and its `should-mock-ai.js` import) beside its only caller, `resolveIssueAccess` in `lib/dispatch-factory.js`**, rather than widening the seal module's header. Reason: the seal module's header then stays true and it holds no test-mode knowledge. The predicate is unexported and had no other caller. Citations made stale by the move (`lib/should-mock-ai.js`, `lib/providers/linear/index.js`, `docs/architecture/source-map.md`) now point at the factory. Blind read, terminology: the `countingProvider` comment and the describe title now say "declared property", not "capability".
- `20199ecd5`, `e82fad67f`, `dd0078a5f` — merges of `origin/main` (LIN-4450 and LIN-4454 landed, then LIN-4457) to clear conflicts in `docs/architecture/source-map.md` and `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md`. In the area note I kept Waiting #8's removal and let piece 7's own removal of the `cost-read` entry stand. One slip: `e82fad67f` pushed with conflict markers left in the area note; `dd0078a5f` removed them, a check I ran found them before CI ran, and the markers never reached `main`.
- Checks run locally on each head: the `as-asked*`, `dispatch-issue-access`, `should-mock-ai`, docs and area-note suites, all passing.

### Ledger
Empty, as recorded by review. Nothing to settle. Review's mutation checks (flag removed, token-only predicate, name check restored, skip removed) each turned a witness red; I did not re-run them after the predicate moved, because the logic is unchanged and the same witnesses ran green in CI on the merged head.

### Blind read
- Inside, fix-sized (header ownership, "capability" wording): fixed above.
- Inside, larger (nothing ties the `testTransport` declaration to the transport installers, so they can drift): a `## Waiting` entry in `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md` (first path `lib/dispatch-factory.js`), PR #2428. It is not fixed here: it needs a decision on where test transports register, across providers, web routes and fixtures.
- Review's class finding (about 16 inline `=== 'test-token'` sites): it fails the consequence test (nothing is broken, `isHermeticTestToken` is gated on `NODE_ENV=test`), so a `## Waiting` entry, not a ticket. The notes check requires the first path to map to the note's area, and `routes/proxy-compute.js` maps to agent-api, so the entry is in `docs/areas/agent-api.md`. I missed writing both entries before the merge, which is why they went in as #2428.
- No tickets filed; nothing needed the existing-ticket search.

### After the deploy
None needed. The change takes effect only under `NODE_ENV=test`, and the repo has no deploy workflow. The verification is the unit/E2E suites on the merged commit.

### Left for John
- Ruling `lin4456-testtransport-placement` shows as answered (resolved 2026-11-13T15:33Z); the ruling row I read does not record which option was chosen. What shipped is the `static` placement (the recommended option). If the answer was `installers`, that would reopen this piece, at the cost of the red witness and the LIN-1880 leak the engineering call describes.
- Related tickets: LIN-4447 (parent) stays open for its other pieces. The placement departure is already on LIN-4447 (comment `40d7c83a`).

## Autopilot run summary — LIN-4456 (stepper)

**Outcome:** done. PR #2426 squash-merged as `e8e92d50a`, LIN-4456 is Done.

**Beats (one warm session, 5 beats, implementation kind only)**
1. Re-ground, records, branch: size record `Decided by` updated (the record format accepts only three fixed values, so it reads "the standing policy"; the 44b575a3 citation is in the LIN-4447 comment 40d7c83a), branch created from origin/main.
2. Witnesses first: new stand-in witnesses added; (a) red on unchanged code. (c) cannot go red on the old name check, so mutation checks stood in (skip removed leaks to api.linear.app:443; token-only keying turns (b) red).
3. Implement: `testTransport` declared once on `LinearProvider`; factory skips access only on declared property + hermetic token. Access suite 10/10, broader run 186 files / 4296 tests green, declaration-removal mutation red then restored.
4. Docs: Waiting #8 removed, source-map reworded, Lessons 4,269 B (< 6,144).
5. Push, PR #2426, 8/8 CI checks green, Linear comment 08275095.

**Then:** review (Approve, conditional on two comment fixes, empty ledger, own mutation checks) → blind-read ("same"; 2 fix-sized, 1 larger find) → close-out (merge, fixes, ticket Done).

**Evidence I checked myself**
- PR #2426 MERGED, merge commit `e8e92d50a`; Tests run on it: success. Close-out says CI was 8/8 green on the pinned head `dd0078a5f`.
- On main: no conflict markers in the five touched files, no `provider.name === 'linear'` left, `testTransport` present on the provider and in the factory.
- Docs-only follow-up PR #2428 merged (`0092d8d9e`); its post-merge Tests run was still in progress when I looked.

**Worth knowing**
- A merge commit during close-out briefly pushed conflict markers into the area note on the PR branch; the next commit removed them and they never reached main.
- Close-out filed the blind read's larger find (nothing links the Linear flag to the transport installers) and the ~16 inline `'test-token'` sites as Waiting entries in docs-only PR #2428, after the main merge instead of before it. No tickets filed; neither breaks anything today.
- Ruling `lin4456-testtransport-placement` shows answered but does not record the option picked; what shipped is the recommended `static` placement, which is the settled engineering call.

description:
## As asked

**Parent:** LIN-4447 (Runs & dispatch, left simpler). The parent's scope is its `## As asked` block. Its approved design and plan are the `## Design` and `## Implementation Plan` sections of the parent description, and the Design comment (6efb91fa) holds the full analysis. **Start from the parent's approved plan and follow it. Where the code shows it is wrong, change course and say so in a comment on LIN-4447.**
**Repository:** JKershaw/LinearViewer. **Grounding commit:** `origin/main` 4b5001ddf. On 2026-11-13 at 14:00Z it was still HEAD, with nothing landed since the ticket was filed.

## Piece 6 (small): test transport keyed on a declared capability

**Correction the plan already made to the Design:** keying on `isHermeticTestToken` alone is wrong. The comment at `lib/dispatch-factory.js:925-934` (check at line 948: `access.provider.name === 'linear' && isHermeticTestToken(access.token)`) records that only Linear's transport is swapped under test. Other providers take `test-token` as a working credential, and the seal and file-pointer suites rely on that.

**Approach:**

* A provider declares `testTransport` where its transport is swapped: Linear, in `routes/test.js` and `tests/fixtures/hermetic-linear.js`.
* The factory skips access only for `provider.testTransport && isHermeticTestToken(token)`.
* Do not remove a non-Linear provider's access merely because it uses `test-token`.

**Retires:** the `provider.name === 'linear'` test and the "this is not a capability" comment. **Settles Waiting:** 8.

**Testing / witness:**

* Linear with the test token has no access.
* An ordinary local provider with the same token still has access.
* A stand-in provider that declares the capability is skipped.
* The seal and file-pointer suites stay green.

Session fit: fits one session
Plan-review due: no — covered by LIN-4447's approving plan-review (comment 12619798-1986-467f-b67c-8bed766a7813, rev 2)

**Binding for every piece (from the parent's Constraints):** compute readiness from the trail on read and never store it. Add no GitHub or provider reads. In the same change, remove the Waiting entries this piece settles and any stale Lesson clause in `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md`, and keep Lessons under 6,144 bytes. Say in the PR what this piece retires. Never recompute stored pre-cutover history, and never edit recorded prompt changelog text. The LLM & prompts side of the seam belongs to LIN-4448 (A14).

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Size of the move

**Size:** just the task
**Why:** Delivers the asked skip as a fixed fact of the Linear provider rather than a flag set by test setup, so tests without an installed transport stay off the network; no survey finding binds a larger move.
**Cuts:**

* "A provider declares `testTransport` where its transport is swapped: Linear, in `routes/test.js` and `tests/fixtures/hermetic-linear.js`." Declared on the Linear provider instead.

**Decided by:** a ruling

## Implemented (close-out stub)

Implemented in [PR #2426](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2426>) (squash `e8e92d50a`; wording fixes and the predicate move `ecd7e7d30`) with Waiting entries in [PR #2428](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2428>) (squash `0092d8d9e`). `LinearProvider` declares `testTransport` once in its constructor and `refusesHermeticToken` in `lib/dispatch-factory.js` skips access only for that property together with the hermetic `test-token`. The plan was implemented as approved, with one departure: the declaration is on the provider, not at the transport installers (engineering decision, comment 44b575a3; noted on LIN-4447, comment 40d7c83a). The full history is preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.
